newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 10 people killed in Somalia militia fighting.
newsitem.headline: 10 people killed in Somalia militia fighting.

text.p: Ten people were killed and 16 injured in overnight fighting between militia loyal to rival faction leaders Ali Hassan Osman Atto and Hussein Aideed in southern Somalia, militia leaders said on Friday.

They said Aideed's militia attacked a militia base occupied by Atto fighters in Magambo, Lower Juba region, 450 km (280 miles) southeast of Mogadishu and seized the base. They added that Atto's men were now fighting to recapture it.

Mahmoud Mohamed, commander of Hussein Aideed's militia in the capital Mogadishu, said his men also seized two "technical" army wagons from Atto's militiamen. He gave no further details on the fighting.

The fighting this week was the bloodiest flare up since Somali factions -- including Atto and Aideed -- agreed in Nairobi two weeks ago to end hostilities, remove roadblocks and pledged a continuation of dialogue for a peace process. The peace deal was brokered by Kenyan President Daniel arap Moi.

Ahmed Ali, a radio operator based in Magambo, said fighters were using heavy and small arms and fighting was continuing. He said 30 families loyal to Atto had been forced out of the Magambo area. The wounded were taken to the Kismayu hospital.
This week has seen dozens of deaths in Mogadishu alone.
On Wednesday, 26 people were killed and 48 wounded when Atto forces attacked and captured an airstrip from Aideed fighters.
Since last month supporters of Aideed have killed more than 10 people who backed Atto, a rival south Mogadishu faction leader whose forces are widely blamed for killing Farah Aideed.
Aideed, like his father, was elected president of Somalia by supporters and heads a government. But it has not received much international recognition and is rejected by most other leaders.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow by rebels of late dictator president Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991.
